# Provider compatibility

Last reviewed: 2026-10-23.

Statuses:
- **implemented and tested**
- **implemented, not integration-tested**
- **planned**
- **unsupported**: the provider offers it, but the toolkit does not implement it
- **unavailable from provider**

**No adapter has been run against a live provider account.** Every row below marked "implemented" is tested against protocol fixtures built from the official docs (and, for signatures, generated by the official SDKs), so under the statuses above all are **implemented, not integration-tested**.

Codec, direction and playback facts per provider:

| Provider | Directions | Bidirectional | Codec / rate | Playback & interruption |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Twilio | inbound, outbound tracks | `<Connect><Stream>` only | μ-law 8 kHz mono | `media`, `mark`, `clear` |
| Plivo | `inbound`, `outbound`, `both` | `bidirectional=true` (inbound only) | L16 8/16/24 kHz, μ-law 8 kHz | `playAudio`, `checkpoint`, `clearAudio` |
| Telnyx | inbound, outbound (`stream_track`) | `stream_bidirectional_mode=rtp`, one per call | PCMU, PCMA, L16 (G722/OPUS/AMR-WB refused) | `media`, `mark`, `clear` |
| Vonage | one mixed stream | always | L16 LE 8/16/24 kHz | binary audio, `notify`, `clear` |

### Behaviour shared by all JSON adapters

- **`bidirectional`:** neither provider says in-band whether a stream is bidirectional. Hosts pass `bidirectional` when creating the session. Until they do, playback capabilities stay `requires_configuration` and raise `invalid_configuration` with the reason.
- **Unknown future event types:** ignored and counted (`ignoredMessages`), so new provider messages don't break live calls.
- **Malformed input:** messages that are malformed, out of order, for another stream or oversized raise typed `ProviderError`s. The session stays in its previous state.
- **Slow consumers:** when the consumer falls behind, audio frames are dropped and counted (`droppedAudioFrames`). Control events are never dropped silently.

## Twilio Media Streams: protocol notes

Sources: [Media Streams overview](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/media-streams), [WebSocket messages](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/media-streams/websocket-messages), [Webhook security](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/webhooks/webhooks-security).

- **From Twilio:**
  - `connected`, then `start` (once), `media`, `stop`.
  - `dtmf` and `mark` arrive on bidirectional streams only.
  - Numeric-looking fields (`sequenceNumber`, `media.chunk`, `media.timestamp`) arrive as strings and must be parsed.
- **Audio:**
  - `start.mediaFormat` is always `audio/x-mulaw`, 8000 Hz, 1 channel.
  - `media.payload` is base64.
  - `media.timestamp` is ms since stream start, which maps to `timestampKind: "stream_relative_ms"`.
- **Tracks:** `start.tracks` lists `inbound` and/or `outbound`. Each `media` message carries `media.track`.
- **To Twilio (bidirectional only):**
  - `media`: raw μ-law/8000 base64 with no file header bytes.
  - `mark`: echoed back when playback reaches it, or when cleared.
  - `clear`: flushes buffered audio, and Twilio then returns pending marks.
- **Modes:**
  - `<Connect><Stream>` is bidirectional and blocks subsequent TwiML until the stream ends.
  - Unidirectional streams are inbound-only to the app; they cannot play audio, receive marks or receive DTMF events.
- **Auth:**
  - Webhooks use `X-Twilio-Signature`, an HMAC-SHA1 of the exact URL plus sorted POST params, keyed by the auth token.
  - JSON bodies are covered by a `bodySHA256` query param.
  - Twilio's docs state the Media Streams WebSocket handshake carries the signature as lowercase `x-twilio-signature`. This needs fixture verification in Phase 3 before `stream_auth_validation` is declared supported.
- `start.customParameters` carries `<Parameter>` values from TwiML.

## Plivo Audio Streams: protocol notes

Sources: [Audio Streams API](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice/api/audio-streams), [Stream event protocol](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice-agents/audio-streaming/concepts/stream-event-protocol), [Audio streaming concepts](https://docs.plivo.com/docs/voice/concepts/audio-streaming).

- **Start via REST:**
  - Endpoint: `POST /v1/Account/{auth_id}/Call/{call_uuid}/Stream/` with HTTP Basic auth.
  - Parameters: `service_url`, `bidirectional`, `audio_track`, `stream_timeout`, `content_type`, `status_callback_url`, `extra_headers`, `noise_cancellation` (`"true"`/`"false"`) and `noise_cancellation_level` (60–100, default 85).
  - The stream can also be started from XML `<Stream>`.
- **`content_type`:** `audio/x-l16;rate=8000|16000|24000` or `audio/x-mulaw;rate=8000`.
- **Constraint:** `bidirectional=true` requires `audio_track=inbound`. The capability model expresses this as `requires_configuration`.
- **From Plivo:**
  - `start` carries `callId`, `streamId`, `accountId`, `tracks` and `mediaFormat`.
  - `media` carries `track`, `timestamp`, `chunk` and `payload`.
  - Also `dtmf`, `playedStream` and `clearedAudio`.
  - `extra_headers` arrives as a string on `start`, `media` and `dtmf`.
  - `sequenceNumber` and `chunk` are JSON numbers, unlike Twilio's strings.
  - `media.timestamp` is documented as Unix epoch ms, which maps to `timestampKind: "unix_epoch_ms"`.
- **To Plivo:**
  - `playAudio` with `media.contentType`, `media.sampleRate` and `media.payload`; it must match the stream's format.
  - `checkpoint` (with `streamId` and `name`), `clearAudio` (with `streamId`) and `sendDTMF`.
- **Provider-native noise suppression:** available at stream start. The planned adapter will declare it `supported` under `provider_noise_suppression` and report it apart from the toolkit's own pipeline.
- **Auth:** HTTP callbacks use `X-Plivo-Signature-V3` and `X-Plivo-Signature-V3-Nonce`, an HMAC-SHA256 over method, full URL and nonce. The docs do not clearly state whether the WebSocket handshake is signed.

### Open questions to resolve before the Plivo adapter ships

1. **`start` sequence number:** Plivo's pages disagree on whether `sequenceNumber` on `start` is 0 or 1. The adapter must accept both, and fixtures must cover both.
2. **WebSocket `stop`:** a `stop` event is not documented; only the `stopped` status callback is. Until one is confirmed, the adapter will treat socket close as `stream_stopped` with reason `socket_closed`.
3. **WebSocket handshake signature:** whether the handshake carries `X-Plivo-Signature-V3`. If it doesn't, `stream_auth_validation` is `requires_configuration`, meaning a shared secret in `extra_headers` or the URL, as configured by the host.
4. **`playAudio` sample rate type:** the API page shows `sampleRate` as a string, while the event-protocol page shows a number. The adapter will send a number and verify against a live account before declaring playback `implemented and tested`.
